topics.flagship-ru-ua: Trump, Xi and Putin held what AP called their first-ever three-way meeting in Shenzhen. Their 'peace declaration' reportedly left out the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Other reports say 200+ meters of the Crimea Bridge are wrecked, creating a logistics problem for Russia. Elbridge Colby was rebuked by NATO allies after saying Ukraine's deep strikes haven't shortened the war. Poland reportedly foiled a Russian 'false flag' plot near Kaliningrad, and a BBC report describes fighting in a Soviet-era tunnel in Kharkiv region.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Trump said Iran may be exploring biological and chemical weapons and urged Americans not to panic over reports of a possible attack on Washington. Iran's parliamentary speaker dismissed reports of a 'dirty bomb' plot as 'false flags'. Trump also said the US will 'see what happens' after Jan. 1, and the US warned Americans in the Middle East of possible attacks and flight disruptions. Israeli tanks reportedly crossed Gaza's ceasefire 'yellow line', displacing Palestinians and straining the truce. A suspected Houthi missile hit the Saudi Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh.
topics.T15: Storms that brought record rain to South Florida moved north to the Space Coast, prompting water rescues of people and horses. Seminole County reported roads and homes flooding as Lake Harney reached major flood stage. Elsewhere, Los Angeles-area evacuation warnings were issued for rain, a landfill gas eruption at Chiquita Canyon sent workers to hospitals, Bhubaneswar activated cyclone shelters ahead of Cyclone Akvan, and Tonga declared a nationwide drought emergency.
topics.T01: Somalia ordered the UAE ambassador to leave, citing an 'invasion', according to a single report. A Saudi airstrike on a hotel in Mocha, Yemen reportedly killed at least nine civilians, per the Sanaa-based Health Ministry. Myanmar's military reportedly bombed a displaced persons camp in Rakhine State, killing 12 civilians. All three are single-source reports.
topics.T02: Coverage of the ICJ genocide ruling on the Rohingya (10 outlets) leads the topic, with the court described as ruling for the first time that a state committed genocide. A PRIO/Save the Children report estimates 589 million children lived in conflict zones in 2025, a record. Other items cover Bhotekoshi flood victims still awaiting aid in Nepal, Ukrainian displaced persons' housing struggles, and Yemen's Bab al-Mandab crossing becoming more dangerous.
topics.T03: Trump said there are indications Iran may be looking at biological weapons and threatened to 'wipe out' Iran if it attacks. One outlet noted Tehran's capabilities remain unclear, and the available coverage presents no confirmed evidence. The claims are linked to reported fears of an attack on US soil and concern about the new year.
topics.T04: Coverage is scattered, with no single dominant outbreak. Items include a Covid inquiry report urging UK–Ireland pandemic coordination, a Legionnaires' disease outbreak that killed two, draft Indian quarantine rules for unvaccinated yellow fever-risk travellers, and screwworm quarantines in parts of Texas's Brooks and Kenedy counties after larvae were found in Hidalgo County. The rest is retrospective academic research.
topics.T05: Japan's prime minister received a frosty reception on a China visit after saying an attack on Taiwan could trigger a Japanese deployment. A Florida pastor was convicted over the plot that killed Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. A Pakistani minister is to visit India for an SCO forum, though analysts expect no breakthrough. An Indian opposition party questioned the RSS chief's Manipur visit. No coup-type events appear in this coverage.
topics.T06: Hundreds of Iranians reportedly chanted 'Death to the dictator!' in Abdanan after a bus crash killed 13 refinery workers, with at least seven arrests. Haredi crowds clashed with police in Beit Shemesh. Bangladesh riots reportedly saw Muhammad Yunus's home set on fire. UK coverage includes Farage warning of riots over Brexit and a retailer citing 'civil unrest' in Europe.
topics.T07: Coverage of the Trump-Xi-Putin summit (6 outlets) described the unprecedented meeting as spanning nuclear risks to energy flows. The US, UK, France and Germany demanded Iran restore IAEA access, warning that its enriched uranium stockpile is unverified. IAEA chief Rafael Grossi's bid for UN secretary-general is also covered.
topics.T08: Nigeria's army said an airstrike killed 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno, and troops foiled an attack in Zamfara. A GAO test found four major AI chatbots produced feasible terror-attack plans after safeguards were bypassed. Syria's Christian leaders warned of a 'grave' threat amid attacks and kidnappings. Bukele reportedly confirmed an airstrike on a Haitian gang leader's mansion, and a Sinaloa cartel bombing killed one man.
topics.T09: The husband of Olga Jezler, an American detained in Russia for over four years, said her case was not raised in Trump's meeting with Putin. Marco Rubio announced the release of an American child kidnapped in Haiti.
topics.T10: Venezuela signed a military deal with the US, which the US defense secretary described as moving Venezuela from regional threat to 'compliant security partner'. Appropriators reportedly cut Trump's $17B Golden Dome request in a draft bill, and Trump announced $17B in Asia deals including defense. Other items cover a British Navy helicopter being converted into a 'drone mothership', China's reported effort to obtain Nvidia chips, and the Pentagon's ninth failed audit.
topics.T11: India and Malaysia began exercise Harimau Shakti on Nov. 19, to run through Nov. 30 with 120 personnel each, focused on counter-terrorism and drone/counter-drone operations. India also held bilateral naval exercises with Canada (INS Sahyadri/HMCS Regina) and Myanmar (IMNEX-26). US and allied forces wrapped two weeks of island-hopping war games in Hawaii, described as preparation for a possible fight with China.
topics.T12: The European Commission is reportedly scrambling to contain an AI-assisted cyberattack that took HR and medical reimbursement systems offline. Equinor is battling a cyberattack, though oil and gas production is reportedly unaffected. Ukrainian government websites were reportedly forced offline. Officials said 'cyber malicious activity' was not tied to recent US outages, and incident responders reportedly report surging AI-enabled attacks. Ukraine also arrested four members of a ransomware gang that took $40.5M.
topics.T13: Five EU nations reportedly moved forward on a plan to deport failed asylum seekers to Rwanda. Other items are largely opinion or partisan outlet pieces on Spanish and Danish migration politics and UK demographics, and they are too thin and one-sided to support a coherent summary.
topics.T14: A single, partisan-outlet report says US embassies issued a Europe-wide terror alert ahead of Christmas, citing the UK's 'severe' threat level. Nothing else is available to corroborate or detail it.
topics.T16: Coverage is sparse and mixed. Items include analysis of the 2026 US midterms, where Democrats won a 'blue wave' and more than 30 House Republican incumbents lost, plus Canadian by-elections on Dec. 7 and B.C. Conservative MLAs being sworn in. Spain's general election is set for Nov. 29, and Nigeria's APGA adopted Tinubu for 2027. No electoral-integrity incidents are reported.

bluf: The ICJ ruling on the Rohingya, described across 10 outlets as the first time the court has found a state committed genocide, was the most widely covered development. Trump, Xi and Putin held what AP called their first-ever three-way meeting in Shenzhen, but their 'peace declaration' reportedly left out the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Trump said Iran may be exploring biological weapons and that the US would 'wipe them out', while urging Americans not to panic over reports of a possible attack on Washington; coverage shows no confirmed evidence. Israeli tanks reportedly crossed the Gaza ceasefire 'yellow line', displacing Palestinians and, per analysts, risking the already fragile truce with Hamas. Storms that brought record rain to South Florida moved to the Space Coast, prompting water rescues of people and horses. Separately, reports say more than 200 meters of the Crimea Bridge have collapsed, creating a logistics problem for Russia. A suspected Houthi missile also hit the Saudi Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh, and the US has warned Americans in the Middle East of possible attacks.
